newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia reconstruction aid conference postponed.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia reconstruction aid conference postponed.

text.p: A fund-raising conference for Bosnia's reconstruction set for next week has been postponed because the peacetime central government failed to adopt economic reforms in time, a World Bank official said on Friday.

"The donors' conference will not take place on June 24 and 25 as we earlier hoped for or planned. Expectations are that it will be held in the middle of July," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

The conference, which was expected to raise $1.4 billion in reconstruction aid in 1997, has been repeatedly postponed because Bosnia's inter-ethnic government has failed to approve a package of economic laws which the international community had set down as a precondition for more aid.

Leaders of Bosnia's Serb republic withrew their support earlier this month for the economic laws which had been agreed after months of negotiations, despite threats they could lose out on substantial financial aid.
Nationalist Serb leaders opposed a proposed customs and tariffs law because they said it violated a cooperation agreement with neighbouring Yugoslavia.
International envoys say the cooperation pact between the Serb entity and Yugoslavia carries no legal validity.
The long-running dispute also sparked disagreements between the United States and European powers, diplomats said.

The United States, trying to make good on warnings issued by major powers last month, had pushed for a postponement of the conference. European states had argued for holding the conference without the Serbs for the sake of the Moslem-Croat federation, which approved the economic laws on time.
The former international High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, said on Thursday that Washington had placed "severe pressure" on his office to postpone the conference.
The World Bank and the European Union, who are sponsoring the conference, were expected to announce the postponement formally later on Friday, the official said.
The Serb refusal to back the customs law also delayed a $100 million deal with the International Monetary Fund which was another pre-condition for the aid conference.
Western officials said they hoped the postponement of the conference would not discourage donor countries from pledging aid to rebuild the country's war-damaged infrastructure.
